key_insight: This paper shows that sparse attention can make high-resolution diffusion-based image/video generation much faster without relying on a specific attention backend. The core idea is to preserve efficiency while reducing the quality loss caused by isolated window-based attention.
problem_solved: It addresses the high compute and memory cost of full attention in Diffusion Transformers for high-resolution visual generation, as well as the trade-off in window attention between efficiency and weak cross-window interaction.
method: Design a backend-agnostic sparse attention strategy that works across different implementation backends.
Reduce attention computation by limiting dense all-to-all interactions while preserving important long-range context.
Improve cross-window information flow so generation remains coherent at high resolutions without the artifacts common in isolated window attention.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to scale generative models to higher resolutions with lower compute costs and better visual quality. It is especially useful for efficient image and video generation deployments where speed, memory, and fidelity all matter.

paper_title: Backend-Agnostic Sparse Attention for Fast High-Resolution Visual Generation
paper_authors: Liao Ma, Jiayi Song, Yunfeng Wu, Songhua Liu, Peilin Zhao
